subject: Gravitas Bank — critical queue choke causing 5xx/latency; contract exposure, exec attention requested
messages:
From: Ops Team <ops@gravitasbank.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 08:12:02 -0000
Subject: Production: API latency and 500s since 02:00 UTC — reserved capacity

Alex / Olga,

We're seeing sustained high p99 latency (2.4s -> 6s) and an uptick in 500s across our production inference routes since ~02:00 UTC. This is for our reserved capacity pool (pool-id: rb-grav-1). Token throughput has dropped ~40% vs committed baseline, and requests are queueing.

Impact: checkout API failures for some users; finance processing jobs delayed. We are tracking increased error rate in the logs (attached sample).

Please advise immediate mitigation steps. If we can't restore baseline QPS by EOD our legal team wants to know potential SLA credit exposure.

Attachments: gravitas_error_trace.log (txt, excerpt), gravitas_dashboard.png (screenshot)

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Platform Ops — Gravitas Bank
ops@gravitasbank.com
(External)

Samir, thank you for the flag — we see the same signal on our side and are treating this as priority.

Immediate next steps I can coordinate now:
- Kick off a 30m triage call with engineering + your ops team (propose 08:45 UTC).
- Temporarily route a small % (10-20%) of Gravitas traffic to a warm failover pool to reduce queueing while we investigate root cause.
- Collect and share token-level traces + KV cache hit stats (sending logs link in follow-up).

Olga, can you join the call and start a capacity check (headroom, active allocations) and prepare burst authorization if we need to push extra instances?

Alex Martinez
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0123

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Gravitas Bank — production degradation; recommended exec bridge and credit discussion

Team — forwarding the customer report (below). Key facts: Gravitas reserved pool rb-grav-1 showing throughput shortfall ~40% vs baseline; p99 increasing and 500s spiking. Customer is explicitly asking about SLA exposure / legal notification if baseline isn't met by EOD.

Ask:
- Ops (Olga): quick health snapshot (headroom, active GPU count, recent autoscale events) and likely root cause (noisy neighbor? kernel selection mismatch? KV cache pressure?).
- Engineering (Rishi): can we author a temporary failover route and enable extra dedicated capacity for 2-4 hours if autoscale won't catch it? Need ETA and required approvals (burst credit / emergency capacity).
- Exec (Vivek): please confirm if we should open an immediate exec bridge and whether we authorize emergency burst credits for Gravitas (they're a high-touch enterprise, DEAL-8471). Legal may request early notice if SLA hit probable.

I'll stand up the triage call at 08:45 UTC and include Gravitas ops.

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 10:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Gravitas Bank — production degradation; recommended exec bridge and credit discussion

On the triage call now with Gravitas ops. Quick notes and what we've seen so far:

Observations:
- Pool rb-grav-1 shows sustained queue depth rise starting 02:10 UTC. Active GPU allocation at 92% for last 3 hours.
- Autoscaler attempted two additional allocations but they failed to reach ready state due to lower GPU headroom in the region (quota pressure).
- KV cache miss rate increased (~15% -> 48%) — suggests recent traffic pattern change (longer prompts) causing higher memory churn.
- No obvious model regression; kernel selection logs show an unusual fallback to a slower execution path for ~30% of requests.

Immediate mitigations we are executing now:
1) Shift 15% of traffic to the warm failover pool (rb-failover-3) — should reduce queue pressure within 5-7 minutes.
2) Open emergency burst authorization request to provision 8 additional GPUs in us-west-2 (GCP) — pending approval from exec for temporary capacity.
3) Enable aggressive KV cache prefetch for Gravitas routes to reduce cache miss tail.

ETA: failover shift in 10m; expected p99 to improve within 15m after shift. If autoscale quota remains constrained, we will need a manual burst (8 GPUs) for ~3-6 hours.

Attachments sent to the customer and internal folder: gravitas_dashboard.png (screenshot), gravitas_error_trace.log, gravitas_mbp_playbook.pdf (mitigation runbook). Link to internal dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/gravitas/queueing-overview

Next steps: Alex to coordinate approval with Vivek for emergency burst credits; Rishi to validate if kernel fallback is a performance regression or expected fallback under memory pressure.

Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 16:18:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Gravitas Bank — production degradation; recommended exec bridge and credit discussion

Thanks for the crisp summary. Two immediate asks:

1) Alex — please draft a one‑pager for the exec bridge (what happened, impact, mitigation, timeline, and proposed customer-facing remediation including credits). I want this brief on my desk in 45 minutes; we'll decide whether to authorize the 8 GPU burst and whether to pre-approve SLA credit up to $X (finance will weight the ask).

2) Legal & PS loop — this is potential contract exposure. Copy Legal (legal@gravitasbank.com) on the customer communication and prepare the contract excerpt that defines SLA credit triggers for throughput/availability. If Gravitas requests early notice of SLA deterioration, we need to preserve evidence and timeline.

Do not promise credits yet — collect the metrics and options. If we can get p99 back within 30 minutes of failover shift, that should avoid credits. If not, we'll escalate.

Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Revenue Officer — Redwood Inference
